basis: Parent proposal only; reviewer executed no namespace/mount/job. Unshare success and MemAvailable25.8GiB are parent observations, not memory admission proof.
policy: WORKTREE and sources remain on real disk. Overlay only newly owned empty unique output directories under real worktree in a private user+mount namespace. This does not retire/delete existing disk data or use iPad/external storage. No original8GiB process/resource/receipt/acceptance requirement is weakened.
probe_preconditions: Parent/child mount namespaces must differ; explicitly make mount propagation private, then verify mountinfo. Mount only normalized no-symlink paths beneath the new owned output root, after same-owner empty-directory/inode/device checks. Never overlay existing output/source directories.

2MiB tmpfs must also bound inode count and controlled path/file count. Filesystem size alone does not give an archive metadata/inode bound. Fixed probe files/path lengths should make worst-case uncompressed tar plus compression overhead demonstrably below20MB.

All namespace/tool/tmpfs/restore work stays within the original8GiB cgroup and swap0. tmpfs size is a maximum, not a reservation; charge RAM output, toolRSS, page/cache overhead, compressor and independent restore buffers together.

Bound all real-disk stdout/stderr/manifests/archive growth before admission using actual free-minus10GB reserve, including atomic partial archive, not just final compressed size. Keep original real-disk guard active. Other writers can still remove headroom; record stop/failure exactly.

Keep collector alive outside the killable tool child. A supervisor timeout/OOM that destroys the mount namespace before archive completion loses final evidence. Ensure stop ordering terminates tool, collects/archives/verifies outputs, then exits/unmounts; whole-scopekill must report evidence loss and cannot yield accepted success.

Archive complete final output trees, including complete proof sessions/reports/JSON and relevant cache outputs. Only a dedicated explicitly classified compiler TMPDIR may be excluded. Do not use broad filename/extension exclusions that erase negative/final evidence.

Before archive creation freeze final outputs and snapshot file identity/content/metadata. Reject unsupported links, special files, path traversal or output paths escaping the namespace. Do not follow source symlinks into unrelated host data.

Write one bounded partial compressed archive on real disk, fsync archive/receipt as appropriate, extract independently into separately bounded RAM restore area, verify complete inventory + per-file hashes + chosen metadata + link targets, then atomically publish archive. Record namespace UID mapping for metadata comparison.

If archive cap/restore/source/output identity check fails, mark job failed and do not silently discard final RAM evidence to manufacture a receipt. The probe size/inode bounds should make cap failure impossible under intended output. A real proof job needs the same provable envelope or a pre-authorized retention fallback before launch.
proof_job_extra_gates: Derive all actual GNAT root/Attest/private-library output and cache/config paths from exact project topology with a unique --subdirs name. No source/cache output elsewhere may escape to real disk unexpectedly. TMPDIR/XDGcache redirects alone are not an exhaustive write-path proof.

Qualify tool-memory plus tmpfs-output plus collection/restore peak; MemAvailable25.8GiB does not extend the8GiB cgroup. A bounded child subbudget can reserve collector headroom, but exact limits/failures must be reported and stricter failure is not failure of the original8GiB target.

Choose tmpfs size/inodes/path limits and archive byte bound such that complete worst-case archive fits20MB, not merely expected compression. Output ENOSPC or inode exhaustion is a failed/unproved probe, not grounds to exclude evidence.
Read back actual bounded parallelism and original proof/check/assertion flags. Filesystem isolation cannot authorize new unbounded-j0 defaults or change source/ghost policy.

After namespace exit, mountpoint report paths are empty. Durable archive/index/restore receipt must be named explicitly. Do not claim those original paths still contain reports or update acceptance readers that require materialized files without an approved exact-source restoration path.
A proof exit0 is insufficient absent complete current-source coverage/report and successful retention validation. Keep original F7/O1/full-domain gates open.
risks_not_eliminated: Host crash/power loss before archive publication can lose RAM-only outputs. Report incomplete execution rather than claiming retained evidence.
OOM/timeout scope-kill cleanup order is a concrete retention risk, not solved by archiving only on normal return.
Changing filesystem/output paths may alter cache reuse and timings; fresh exact-source proof/readback remains mandatory.
